source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
Core transplanting techniques of the System of Rice Intensification (SRI):

Pull only healthy, uniform seedlings from the nursery and transplant them immediately afterward, without letting them dry out or wait.

Transplant young seedlings - ideally younger than 15 days old (a target range of 10-15 days after sowing), rather than the older, roughly 1-month-old seedlings used in conventional transplanting.

Transplant only 1 seedling per hill, rather than clumps of multiple seedlings.

Transplant seedlings fresh and shallow, taking care not to let the roots bend or curl under (avoiding a hooked/"J-shaped" root placement, which happens when seedlings are pushed in too deep or too roughly); roots should be able to spread out naturally.

Use wider spacing than conventional planting: hill spacing of about 25-40 cm between hills, arranged in straight rows with even, uniform spacing between all hills (a square or grid planting pattern), rather than the dense, uneven spacing typical of conventional transplanting.
